projects.tracks: input/output/reasoning/cache-read/cache-write tokens; per-call response_cost; cost breakdown (input/output/cache_read/cache_creation/reasoning); per-model pricing; budgets per key/user/team; cost-weighted routing

value_sources.tokens: API usage object (provider response). Reads OpenAI-style usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens & cache_write_tokens/cache_creation_tokens AND Anthropic-style top-level usage.cache_read_input_tokens/cache_creation_input_tokens (cost_calculator.py:374-397)

projects.data_path: proxy call -> usage parsed from provider response -> cost_per_token()/response_cost() -> StandardLoggingPayload (response_cost + response_cost_breakdown) -> emitted to logging callbacks / DB spend logs -> aggregated for budgets & routing -> UI/spend endpoints
projects.cache_token_handling: KEY: helper assumes prompt_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens (OpenAI convention) and computes regular = max(prompt - cached - cache_creation, 0) to avoid double count (cost_calculator.py:212-215). projects.forecast: not a first-class run-out forecast; budget alerts via spend thresholds
projects.api_price_vs_plan: API-priced cost only (per-token pricing table). No notion of plan-included value; custom pricing/discounts via custom_cost_per_token and (open feature req) deployment discounts.
projects.custom_pricing_currencies: custom_cost_per_token / custom_cost_per_second overrides; prices USD; historical price changes handled by refreshing cost.json map (no time-travel reconciliation in core)
projects.privacy: proxy can run self-hosted/local; logging callbacks optional; success/failure logging configurable; redaction of prompt/responses supported in enterprise

projects.window_model: STRONG. UsagePeriod = Interval (ISO-8601 duration: Day/Week/Month/Year) + Anchor time; GetCurrentPeriodAt(at) returns ClosedPeriod; GetResetTimelineInclusive; OriginalUsagePeriodAnchor + LastReset track drift (usageperiod.go:154,186). Supports rolling anchored windows, not just calendar.
projects.threshold_overage: metered Entitlement: IssueAfterReset (default grant amount+priority re-issued each window), IsSoftLimit (allow access at 0 balance vs hard block), PreserveOverageAtReset (carry negative overage into next window) (metered/entitlement.go:30-49). BalanceWindow{UsageInPeriod, Overage, BalanceAtStart, OverageAtStart} (metered/balance.go:29-43).
projects.double_count_prevention: grant priorities + idempotent balance snapshots; overage preserved rather than re-granted
projects.forecast: not a run-out forecast; reset timeline + balance give deterministic projection
projects.api_price_vs_plan: models entitlements/credits (plan-included value), NOT API dollar cost — pure quota/allowance layer; cost is a separate concern
projects.privacy: self-hostable; events stored in your infra; retention via event store config

issues_prs.note: Edge case: grant expiry coincident with usage-period reset produced wrong balance; adds a clock package to model composite ordering of expiry vs reset.

cross_cutting_answers.a_window_threshold_overage_modeling: OpenMeter is the reference model: UsagePeriod = ISO-8601 Interval + Anchor (rolling anchored windows, GetCurrentPeriodAt/GetResetTimelineInclusive), metered Entitlement with IssueAfterReset (auto re-grant each window), IsSoftLimit (allow-at-zero vs hard block), PreserveOverageAtReset (carry overage across reset), and BalanceWindow{UsageInPeriod,Overage,BalanceAtStart,OverageAtStart}. Lago complements with AlertThreshold{value decimal(30,5), recurring} (UNIQUE recurring-per-alert, SOFT_LIMIT const) and recurring wallet top-ups with min/max credits and negative thresholds (fire before zero). Pattern: separate the window definition (anchor+interval+lastReset) from the allowance (grant/credit) from the policy (soft/hard limit, overage preservation) from the alert (recurring vs one-shot threshold).
cross_cutting_answers.b_api_cost_vs_plan_value_separation: They live in different layers. Lago separates prepaid wallet credits / plan subscription (included value) from pay-in-arrears metered charges (billed overage) — wallets are the allowance, charges are the bill. OpenMeter models only entitlements/credits (plan-included units), deliberately NOT dollar cost. LiteLLM/Helicone model only API dollar cost (pricing table/registry). Helicone PR #5694 adds per-request override headers so the caller can inject the true provider cost when the registry's single rate is wrong (OpenRouter pass-through) — i.e. keep 'registry/list price' and 'actual billed cost' as overridable separate fields. PM implication: store list-price cost and plan-included allowance as distinct ledgers, with an override channel for actuals.
cross_cutting_answers.c_vscode_compact_context_surfacing: vs-context is the template: a single status-bar item `${riskIcon} CTX ${agentLabel} ${pct}%` (or `${n} agents · ${peak}% peak`), risk icon switched at warning=70%/critical=85% thresholds ($(pulse)/$(warning)/$(error)), rich tooltip (hottest agent %, total agents, warning/critical counts), click -> tree focus. Data comes from local agent session logs (percentageOfPrompt per category: system/messages/toolResults/files). BedirT shows a configurable token-count template but no %-of-window. Compact = one % number + risk color + expandable detail.
cross_cutting_answers.d_stale_pricing_and_historical_changes: All use a bundled/generated pricing artifact (LiteLLM cost.json/get_model_cost_map, Helicone packages/cost registry generated per provider incl. buildPricesOpenRouter.py) refreshed by releasing an update — no time-travel reconciliation in core. New/changed models produce zero or wrong cost until the registry is updated (Helicone PR #5743 Kimi K3; LiteLLM issue #32496 fireworks). Mitigations seen: custom_cost_per_token overrides (LiteLLM) and per-request cost override headers (Helicone PR #5694). Historical price changes are handled by re-fetching the current map, not by versioned effective-dated prices.
cross_cutting_answers.e_inclusive_vs_additive_cache_tokens: Direct evidence both ways, explicitly reconciled. LiteLLM: OpenAI prompt_tokens INCLUDES cached_tokens (inclusive) while Anthropic input_tokens EXCLUDES cache (additive); it normalizes Anthropic by ADDING cache tokens (cost_calculator.py:400-404) then computes regular = max(prompt - cached - cache_creation,0) to avoid double count. Helicone: treats sum_prompt_tokens as fresh/uncached and ADDS cache buckets separately, and explicitly SUBTRACTS overlapping 5m/1h buckets from prompt_cache_write_tokens 'to not double count' (index.ts:102-108). Conclusion: providers disagree; a metering layer must (1) detect the convention per provider, (2) normalize to one invariant, (3) subtract any overlapping sub-buckets.
